sections.title: User Management
paragraphs: History (audit trails)
Inactive verses Delete
Permissions
• History tab within navigation (PR history and PO history)
• History tab within PR or PO. NOTES:
• There are a few places in the site where once a configuration i s created, there is no way to delete the configuration; there is only t he ability to inactivate it.
• Example: Users, roles, departments, custom field definitions, e tc. NOTES:
• Allow access to functionality in the system.
• Can be assigned at the role and user level.
• Description of the permission can be found by clicking on the p ermission name.
• If the Override Role checkbox is turned on, this indicates tha t the role‐level or parent‐role settings are overridden for the user or role being edited. NOTES:

sections.title: Roles and use of multiple roles
paragraphs: Adding and editing roles
Viewing user information
• Created to manage users with similar permissions.
• One role must be designated as the default role.
• Recommended to setup approval and buying limits at the role lev el instead of the user level.
• Accessed under: Setup/Organization Structure and Settings/Manage User Roles
NOTES:
• Best practice dictates a main parent role with all sub‐roles ex isting under. The main parent role should be inactive.
• Be cautious when creating roles as they can’t be deleted once c reated, they can only be made inactive but not removed completely.
NOTES:

• To search for users, manually cre ate users, or export users, na vigate to: Site Administration / Manage Users / Search For Users o Export users to view their authe ntication method (LoginXML, Loc al, LDAP, etc.).
NOTES:

sections.title: Adding new users
paragraphs: • Can be added manually by accessing: Site Administration / Manage Users / Add New User (this will create a user with the Local authentication method a ssigned by default.)

• Bulk users can be imported with the appropriate authentication method using the user import feature. A template is provided along with import instructions. Site Administration / Manage Users / Import Users From A File
NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 2: Site Messaging and Customization
paragraphs: Information Boxes and Logo
Admin Home Page
Updating the Organization Message
• Accessed via: Home/Administrator Home

• Admin homepage provides: o Quick link access, handbooks, sol utions portal access, and know ledge base access. o Information on tasks that requir e attention, organization msg, quick access to approvals, price files etc.
NOTES:
• The Organization Message is an important tool for communicating with the user community.
• Administrators must first have th e permission to change the com pany message ( profile > Administrator Permissions > System Administ ration > Edit Company Message ).
• Fully customizable, HTML (bulle ts, fonts, colors, links).
• To update, click on the “update message” link on Shopping or Ad ministrator Home, or under: Setup/Site Appearance And Behavior/ Organization Message And Site Logos
NOTES:

sections.title: System Configuration
paragraphs: Updating Resource Information (phone and email support)
Updating the site logo
Security and sessi ons configuration
• Gives end users an email/numbe r to call with questions/issues.
• Administrators must first have th e permission to edit the resou rce information (profile > Administrator Permissions > System Administration > Edit Resource Information ).
• To update; Setup/ Site Appearance And Behavior/Organization Message And Site Logos
NOTES:
• Upload the image under: Setup/ General Site Settings / Manage Organizational Images
• Associate the image as the organization logo under: Setup/ Site Appearance And Behavior/Organization Message And Site Logos
NOTES:
• Administrators must first have th e permission to access and edi t system configuration settings ( profile > Administrator Permissions > System Administration > System Conf iguration).
• Accessed Under: Setup/ General Site Settings / System Settings and Configuration: Security and Sessions
• Pertains to Local login users (mostly administrators).
• Timeouts, password expirat ion, registration, etc. NOTES:

sections.title: Appearance & International Settings
paragraphs: Miscellaneous Settings
EMail Settings & Email Addresses
• Admins can set defaults for the organization under: Setup/ General Site Settings / System Settings and Configuration
Appearance: o Color Theme, Font Size, Help on mouse over International Settings: o Language, Country, Time Zone NOTES:
Setup/ General Site Settings / System Settings and Configuration: Misc Settings

Setup/ General Site Settings / System Settings and Configuration: Email Settings o Include PR & PO notes in Email o Exclude URL links in Do cument‐based emails o Preferred email format o Send expiration notifications for inactive contracts Setup/ General Site Settings / System Settings and Configuration: Email Addresses

sections.title: User Communication
paragraphs: Terms And Conditions (User)
Email Users
Cart Reminder Settings

Setup/ User Communication / Site Terms And Conditions o Functionality for an end‐user disclaimer prior to using the app lication. o Customizable message to be displayed to end users. o Before accessing, end us er must agree to the terms, if they agr ee, they get access, if they don’t agree, they are returned to the login screen. o JAGGAER – Campus Admin access ible, should be Global Admin only.

sections.title: Field Management
paragraphs: Navigating in Field Management
Field Management via the site and via the search
Updating field labels
• Accessed under: Setup/ Field Management / Manage Field Names And Help Text
• Administrators must first have th e permission to access and edi t field management ( profile > Administrator Permissions > System Administration > Field Management ).
• Search using “Search:” area and inputting the application text to be changed.
• The navigation path for a field is shown on the left side of th e screen.
• Once selected, the field attr ibutes (visible, required, display name, help text etc.) are displayed/editable on the right side of the screen.
NOTES:
• You can also search for fields via the quick search in the top right of the application by selecting “Field Display Name”.
• Accessing fields via the GUI – Cl icking on the label hyperlink will route you to the field in field mgt.
• Note: Some “phrases” in the applic ation email notifications can be searched for and modified.
NOTES:
• Once selected, field attributes such as; Visible, Required, Dis play Name & Help Text can be “overridden” by checking the corresponding check box and making/saving the modi fications.
NOTES:

sections.title: Making fields visible/not visible and required/optional
paragraphs: Updating help text
Saving Field Management changes
Field Thesaurus
• Some but not all fields can hav e their visibility and required attributes changed. This will depend on the field and the system set‐up/enabled functionality. NOTES:
• Great way to educate users!
• Default help text is provided by JAGGAER, administrators can ad d/change/delete help text.
• Can use HTML, up to 1,000 characters.
• Example: Shopping Home > click on any question mark ‐> click on “edit in field management” hyperlink. NOTES:
• After overriding/editing a field attribute, click “Save”
• Changes will be immediate in the application. NOTES:
• Accessed Under: Setup/ Field Management / Configure Field Thesaurus
• Allows modification to common “key” terms
• Reduces the amount of sear ching and editing required
• Will address a majority of the oc currences of the term, however there maybe additional modifications required. NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 3: Custom Field Management
paragraphs: Creating Custom Fields and Custom Field Values
Creating and activating custom fields
Defining values for custom fields – loaded to site manually or via import

• Administrators must first have th e Custom Field Management perm ission enabled to create and edit custom fields and values ( profile > Administrator Permissi ons > System Administration > C ustom Field Management ).
• Accessed Under: Setup/ Configure Documents / Manage Custom Fields o Custom Field Style can be: Yes/No, Organization‐wide List or U se User Profile Permissions.
NOTES:
• To define custom field values, navigate to: Setup/ Configure Documents / Manage Custom Fields > Values Tab o Select existing Custom Field, use “Create New Value “ button

• To load custom field values v ia an import, navigate to: Setup/ Configure Documents / Manage Custom Fields > Import/Export Tab o Custom fields can also be loaded through the custom field impor t integration.
NOTES:

sections.title: Determining custom field placement
paragraphs: Understanding and defining parent/child relationships for custom fields
Creating parent/child values
Completing setup using document design
• Determines where on the requisitio n and/or the PO, the field wi ll reside.

• Accessed Under: Site Configuration/ Configure Documents / Manage Custom Fields > Placement Tab o Can specify “required at checkout” or “display order” o Only fields in the “Codes” secti on can be used for Accounting C odes NOTES:
• One to many relationship, parent custom fields can have many ch ildren.

• Accessed Under: Site Configuration/ Configure Documents / Manage Custom Fields > Paren t‐Child Relationships Tab o The parent/child relationship struct ure must be defined here be fore values can be added(Parent‐Child Values)
NOTES:
• Once the parent/child relationship has been defined, values can be associated.
• Accessed Under: Site Configuration/ Configure Documents / Manage Custom Fields > Parent‐Child Values Tab
NOTES:
• Custom Fields can be used to def ine the look of the PR, PO docu ment, and faxes sent to suppliers.
• Accessed Under: Site Configuration/ Configure Documents / Configure (Requisition/Purchase Order) Document
NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 4: Workflow Administration
paragraphs: Financial Workflow Permissions related to financial workflow
Assigning financial approvers to users
• Allows organizations to trigger approvals based on a user’s fin ancial limits.
• The purchasing approval limits determine when a user requires f inancial approval (include line‐level limit, total requisition limit , PCard limit, etc.).
• Access a user’s purchasing/approval limits under: profile > User Access and Security > User Purchasing and Approval Limit Values. NOTES:
• Can assign approvers to users or allow users to determine who c an approve their orders.
• JAGGAER must first turn on the Financial Approvers setting in o rder for this functionality to become available to an organization.
• Financial Approvers can be setup under: profile > User Information and Settings > Financial Approvers. NOTES:

sections.title: Static Workflow
paragraphs: Viewing static shared workflow folders
Adding approvers to static shared workflow folders
• When static workflow steps are created, one or more shared work flow folders are created.
• Access shared workflow folders for purchase requisitions under: Site Configuration / Workflow Setup / Requisition Workflow Setup / R equisition Workflow Folders
• Access shared workflow folders for purchase orders under: Site Configuration / Workflow Setup / Purchase Order Workflow Setup / Purchase Order Workflow Folder s
NOTES:
• Approvers are added to Shared Wo rkflow Folders by accessing the folder and selecting the “Add Approvers” button.

• Shared Workflow Folders can be set to “Enable Automatic Approval” which means the step in workflow will be automatically approved if the order was subm itted by an approver of this step. Note that automatic approvals only consider the ‘Submitted by’ individual
NOTES:

sections.title: Dynamic Workflow
paragraphs: Advanced Dynamic Workflow
Assigning approvers to objects driving dynamic workflow (e.g. custom field values, form types, departments)
Creating Advanced Dynamic Workflow Rules

• Dynamic Workflow involves assigni ng Approvers to “objects” with in the system, such as: Custom Field values, Departments, Form types, Commodit y Codes, Contract Types etc. o Dynamic Workflow can be set for t he Requisition, PO & Invoice l evels of the object. o Dynamic Workflow uses Rules that can “Route All” or only be tri ggered by value ranges for the Document. o If enabled, “Enable Automatic Approvals” will automatically approve the step if the order was submitted by an appr over of this step.
• After adding and saving a rule for t he object and Approver can be assigned using the “add approver…” link.
NOTES:
• To access advanced dynamic workf low, users must have the approp riate permission: profile > Permission Settings > Administrator Permissions: System Administration ‐ Advanced Dynamic Workflow .
• ADW uses Rule Groups which can h ave one or more rules assigned: o All rules within a Rule Group will be evaluated. o Inactive rules WILL NOT be evaluated.
• Access ADW for requisitions under: Site Configuration > Workflow Se tup > Requisition Workflow Setu p > Requisition Advanced Dynamic Workflow
• Access ADW for purchase orders under: Site Configuration > Workflow Se tup > Purchase Order Workflow S etup > Purchase Order Advanced Dynamic Workflow

• ADW allows System Administrators to define and modify system wo rkflow at any time using Document and Line Level rules based on defined elements . The elements available to eva luate will depend on the document type (PR, PO etc.)
• Both Document and Line Level rules can be defined, all define d rules must evaluate TRUE in order to trigger the rule.
NOTES:

sections.title: Assigning approvers to Advanced Dynamic Workflow Rules
paragraphs: Import/Export of Advanced Dynamic Workflow Rules
• Approvers are assigned on the individual rules by using the “Add Approver…” button.

• Implicit Approvers: Implicit approvers do not have direct approval authority, but will have their orders implicitly approved. Implicit approvers do not receive email no tifications for documents pending in the workflow rule folder, and the wor kflow folder does not appear i n their listed approval folders.
• Rules without Approvers assigned WILL NOT be evaluated.
NOTES:
• Accessed under: Site Configuration > Workflow Setup > (PR or PO) Workflow Setup > (PR or PO) Advanced Dynamic Workflow > Import And Export Rules
• ADW Rules can be exported, validated or imported in Tab Delimited Text or XML formats.
• ADW Import Instructions and Im port Templates are available on t he “Import And Export Rules” tab
NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 5: Forms Management
paragraphs: Form Types and Dynamic Workflow Creating a new form type
Assigning approvers to a form types (Dynamic Workflow)
• New form types can be created under: Site Administration > Shopping Settings > Manage Form Types
• Form Types allow you to group “ like” forms for workflow purpose s. NOTES:
• Depending on the workflow configured by JAGGAER, forms can be a ssigned approvers for the Requisition, PO or Invoice.
• Select the form type and create a new workflow rule, then add a pprovers.
• The form type workflow rules can also be imported > exported un der: Site Administration > Shopping Settings > Manage Form Types: CSV Workflow Rule Import > Export NOTES:

sections.title: Forms Design
paragraphs: Editing an existing form
Designing a New Form (Legacy)
Legacy Forms vs. Form Requests
• To manage forms, navigate to: Site Administration > Shopping Settings > Manage Form > Form R equest Templates
• To make changes to a current ver sion, click the DRAFT option.
• Save changes to the DRAFT vers ion by choosing the Finalize conf iguration version option. Once the version is finalized, select the Activate option.
NOTES:
• A new form can be designed from scratch or created using a temp late.
• To build a new form from scratch, navigate to: Site Administration > Shopping Settings > Manage Form > Form R equest Templates
• Select the “Build a New Form” button.
• To create a new form using a t emplate, select the Template to u se rather than the d efaulted “Blank Form”
NOTES:
• A new form can be designed from scratch or created using a temp late.
• To build a new form from scratch, navigate to: Site Administration > Shopping Settings > Manage Form/Form Requ est Templates
• Select the “Build a New Form Request” button.
• To create a new form using a t emplate, select the Template to u se rather than the d efaulted “Blank Form”
NOTES:

sections.title: Organizational Forms
paragraphs: Setting up and organizing as favorites Saving supplier name with a form
• Once a form is activated, select the “add to favorites” Button. The system administrat or can add the form to the Organization Forms folder to be available for all users. NOTES:
• A form can be used for a specific Supplier by choosing “Limit s upplier selection” under “Form Properties” and adding a supplier. NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 6: Supplier Management
paragraphs: Managing Suppliers
Supplier types (hosted, punch-out, non-catalog)
Searching for suppliers
Making suppliers active/inactive
• Hosted:
• PunchOut:
• Non‐Catalog: NOTES:
• Navigate to: Site Administration/Supplier Management/Search For A Supplier
• Use the “Advanced search” link t o narrow search for active supp liers, PunchOut/hosted/non‐catalog supplier. NOTES:
• After locating the Supplier, toggle suppliers on/off by clickin g on the active or inactive icons:
• Alternatively, go into supplier’s profile, General tab, and ove rwrite the “Enable” attribute. NOTES:

sections.title: Updating basic supplier/information and contact information
paragraphs: Defining purchase order delivery
Overriding standard payment methods for a supplier
• Information inherits from JAGGAER defaults. Click on “Edit” on any value to overwrite with organization‐ specific information.
• Supplier information can also be overwritten if the Supplier Sy nch integration is implemented and active.
NOTES:
• Typically handled by JAGGAER Supplier Enablement or Support. Ca n be overwritten if desired: Choose a supplier: Profile > Fulfillment Addresses > Order Distribution
• Adjust cXML, fax, or email as desired.
• Please note that any deviation f rom JAGGAER defaults result in organization taking ownership of any order delivery failures to the supplier.
NOTES:
• Individual suppliers inherit the organization default settings.
• To update an individual supplier: Choose a supplier: Profile > Ful fillment Addresses > Ordering > Payment Method
• Select Payment Method: PO, PCard, VPayment.
• Adjust PCard, CSC Code, and PO Wheel as desired.
NOTES:

sections.title: Overriding tax, shipping, and handling information for a supplier
paragraphs: Overriding standard PO terms and order acceptance instructions for a supplier
Creating fulfillment addresses
Reviewing supplier history (audit trail)
• Individual suppliers inherit the organization default settings.
• To update an individual supplier: Choose a supplier: Profile > Ful fillment Addresses > Ordering > Tax, Shipping, and Handling
• Add tax, shipping fees, or handlin g fees based on either a flat rate, or percentage of order. NOTES:
• Individual suppliers inherit the organization default settings.
• To update an individual supplier: Choose a supplier: Profile > Ful fillment Addresses > Ordering > Terms and Conditions
• Add information including T&Cs, FOB, Payment Terms, etc.
• PLEASE NOTE that not all suppliers receiving orders electronica lly will be able to receive these. NOTES:
• Fulfillment Centers address mult iple locations of a single supplier that organization may be ordering from.
• Under: Choose a supplier: Profile > Fulfillment Addresses: “New Address” button
• Distribution information must be entered for new FC’s in the ev ent it differs from the inherited default. NOTES:
• In all areas of the Supplier Management screens, there are hist ory tabs to serve as an audit trail for changes. NOTES:

sections.title: Category Management
paragraphs: Creating and Using Classes
Overview of JAGGAER category hierarchy
Categories and subcategories (parent/child) Activating/inactivating categories
Supplier Classes
• Navigate to: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Manage Product Categories NOTES:
• Categories have parent/child relationships. Any action against a parent will affect all the subsequent children. NOTES:
• Organizations have the ability to activate or deactivate catego ries available.
• Drill down to the desired level and click to toggle the categor y on or off: NOTES:
• Used to identify different types of suppliers such as Science C atalog, Diversity suppliers, local suppliers, etc. as well as assigning preferential searching. NOTES:

sections.title: Assigning supplier classes to a Supplier
paragraphs: Category Classes
• Navigate to: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Manage Supplier Classes

• Classes must be created/ activ ated here prior to assigning to a supplier. o All the active supplier classes will be in non‐italicized text. o Select an inactive supplier cl ass (italicized) to edit. o Rename the supplier class, upload an image (if desired), set th e search preference (i f desired), check the Active box and click the Save button.
• JAGGAER offers Austin Tetra Dive rsity flags that can be used.
• A Search Preference can be set f or supplier classes to control where they are “weighted” in search results.
• The existing Supplier Classes can be modified (if needed) and u sed or a new Supplier Class can be created by selecting the “ Create New Class/Definition” button.

• Once a Supplier Class is activat ed, it can be assigned to a Sup plier by: o Navigating to: Site Administration/Supplier Management/Search For A Supplier o Choose a supplier: Profile >Show case/Classes>Supplier Classes
• Assign the appropriate class.
NOTES:
• Used to identify categories to control visibility. Once created Category Classes can be assigned to “Product Views”.
• Navigate to: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Manage Category Classes
• Under “Definitions” select a Cate gory Class to rename and activ ate.
• Under “Configuration” select the Class to configure and toggle categories on/off for the particular class.
NOTES:

sections.title: Supplier Showcase
paragraphs: Activating/inactivating categories by Supplier
Adding Suppliers to the showcase
• Navigate to: Site Administration/Supplier Management/Search For A Supplier
• On the Search Results page: Choose the “Select categories” link for the target Supplier.
• From the Status tab; Categories can be toggled on/off using the “Supplier Toggle”. Note: Changes to the top level Category affect all child categories.
• From the Preference tab; Categories can be assigned a “Preferen ce Selection” for search result “weighting”.
NOTES:
• Used to highlight suppliers on the application homepage.
• Accessed Under: Home/Shopping Home: [Manage Showcases]
• Create New Supplier Sticker o Select Style: Multi‐use or Punch‐out o Select Supplier o Display Supplier: Logo or Text o Select Sticker Logo o Type Caption (optional)
• Select Showcase.
NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 7: Advanced User and Supplier Management
paragraphs: User Management
Departments
Positions
Importing user profile information
• Used to categorize users and user data into specific buckets, c ontrols who has access to what.
• Accessed under: Site Configuration/ Organization Structure and Settings / Config ure Departments And Positions
• A user can be assigned multiple r oles but only one department.
• Allow for department approval triggered through workflow.
• Used to provide more granular rep orting (Example: which departm ent is ordering the most)
NOTES:
• Used for a more granular view of user community.
• Accessed under: Site Configuration/ Organization Structure and Settings / Config ure Departments And Positions: Positions Tab
NOTES:
• User information can be imported in tab delimited or xml format through the UI under: Site Administration / Manage Users / Import Users From A File
• User information can be passed fr om the client to JAGGAER durin g user authentication (varies by client, can be LoginXML, User Import, LDA, etc.).
• User’s information that is passe d from the client to JAGGAER (a uthentication other than Local) will have their profile information locked down (not editable).
NOTES:

sections.title: Product Views
paragraphs: Understanding when to create a product view
Understanding the components of a product view
Creating a product view
Assigning a product view

• Used to control what is returned in search results for HOSTED c atalogs based on existing Supplier Classes, Category Classes or Product Fl ags. Can be applied to an organiz ation, role, or individual user. NOTES:
• Supplier Classes and/or Category Cl asses must be created prior to assigning them to a Product View.
• A Product View must then be a ssigned to a role or individual us er in order to take effect. NOTES:
• See “Creating and Using Classes” from Lesson 4.
• Once a Supplier Class has been c reated and assigned, access Pro duct Views under: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Manage Product Views: Create New View Button
• Name the Product View and choose to include or exclude Supplier Classes, Category Classes or Product Flags.
• A Product View must then be a ssigned to a role or individual us er in order to take effect. NOTES:

• To assign for a role, accessed under: Site Configuration/ Organization Structure and Settings / Manag e User Roles o Select the Role to edit and enable the Product View under: Purchasing > Product Views
• For an individual user: Accessed under User Profile > User Access and Security > Product Views . NOTES:

sections.title: Price File Review
paragraphs: Price Sets
Requesting a price file extract
Reviewing a price file
Approving or Rejecting a price file
• Price Sets are analogous to a spec ific price file submitted. Pr ice Sets can include Corporate List Pricing, HigherEd List Pricing, or Customer‐specific pricing.
NOTES:

• Accessed Under: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Hosted Catalog Price Sets o If needed use “Click for Price Set Search” to locate the Price Set o Click on “Extract: Comparison or Single” link. (Comparison is only available for multiple Price Sets)
• “Single” will provide an extract/data for a specific price file , while “Comparison” will compare two different price files.
• Completed Extracts are found under the Price File Review tab.
NOTES:
• Follow the instructions above to extract pricing awaiting revie w.
• Quick View data is found on the Price File Review tab with additional details prov ided in the file “Download File”
• Please note that LIST pricing do es not require review and appro val.
NOTES:
• Follow the instructions above to extract pricing awaiting revie w.
• Click on “Approve” or “Reject” once file is reviewed.
• Price Files are Approved or Rejected in the order they were sub mitted.
• A “Comparison Extract” can be u sed to compare different Price S et Versions to what is currently loaded for that supplier.
NOTES:

sections.title: Auto Approved price files
paragraphs: Science Catalog settings (if applicable)
Assigning contracts to price sets (if applicable)
• LIST pricing is always Auto Approved.
• Price Files that do not require approval will be Auto Approved.

• Requiring price file approval can be set at the Org level under : Site Configuration/ General Site Settings / System Settings and Configuration o Misc Settings: Price files mu st be approved before loading OR o By individual Supplier under: the Supplier Profile > Item/Price > Price Config/List Price .
NOTES:

• If Science Catalog is being use d, you can request that all of t he suppliers in the catalo g be defaulted off or on. A catalog administrator can then toggle individual suppliers of f or on as desired.
NOTES:
• If you are using Contract Manager, you will need to have contra cts created and active in order to associate pricing to that contract.

• Navigate to: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Hosted Catalog Price Sets o Search for the Price file that you wish to associate with a con tract. Click “assign” o Select the desired contract.
• Contracts can also be assigned to price sets from the Contract within Contract Manager.
NOTES:

sections.title: Address Management
paragraphs: Understanding the risks of address management
Making changes to ship to address formats

• It is imperative that any new addresses, or changes to existing address are communicated to your suppliers that receive PO#s electronically. (Please see the doc ument on Best Practices on Shipping Addresses). NOTES:
• If Shipping Addresses are managed within the application, chang es can be made directly in the Address Mgt screens.
• Accessed Under: Site Configuration/ Organization Structure and Settings / Manage Default Addresses
• PLEASE REMEMBER to alert you r suppliers of these changes. NOTES:

sections.title: Lesson 8: Controlling Catalog Attributes
paragraphs: Commodity Codes
Mapping of Commodity Codes
• Accessed under: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Manage Commodity Codes And Mapping: Configuration

• All hosted items available in th e system have a JAGGAER categor y assigned, if desired, Clients can choose to map the category taxonomy with the option of a further mapping to Client defined Commodity Codes.
• “Select to use category mapping functionality” must be enabled to expose related definition and mapping tabs.

• Mapping Types: o Category Name ‐ This option maps the Commodity Code field to the JAGGAER category name. Mapped values can be overridden on the Category Map tab. o Category UN/SPSC ‐ This option maps the Commodity Code field to the JAGGAER category UN/SPSC values. Mapped values can be overridden on the Category Map tab. o Free‐Form Value ‐ This option does not map the Commodity Code field to any value by default. Mappings must be explicitly set up through the UI or by importi ng them. o Value List ‐ This option does not map the Commodity Code field to any value by default. Mappings must be explicitly set up throug h the UI or by importing them. The values for mapping are those defined on the Manage Value List tab.
• Client specific Commodity Codes are defined on the Manage Category/Commodity List tab and can be imported/export on the Commodity Import/Export tab

• Manual mapping of the JAGGAER cat egories takes place on the Category Map tab, where categories are selected and then modified usi ng a Commodity Code that’s has be en previously defined on the Manage Category/Commodity List tab.
• Mapping of the JAGGAER categories can also be imported/exported via the Category Map Import/Export tab, where a link to the import instructions is included.
NOTES:

sections.title: Units of Measure
paragraphs: Mapping Units of Measure
• Accessed under: Site Configuration/ Hosted Catalo g And Ordering Configuration / Manage Commodity Codes And Mapping: UOMs

• The following options are available for Package UOMs outbound t o the ERP under the “Outbound to ERP Integration Value” pulldown: o send system value ‐ Distributes the JAGGAER‐mapped UOM value to the ERP.
